mainTopic: When the לולב is taken on שבת, the פסוקים behind the לולב laws, and whether סוכה and לולב apply at night
overview: This amud begins at the end of רבה's explanation. The רבנן banned taking the לולב on שבת because a person might carry it ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים, and the same fear explains why there is no שופר or מגילה on שבת. The גמרא asks why the first day of סוכות is different. It concludes that on the first day the מצוה is מן התורה even in the גבולין, so the רבנן did not ban it. On the other days the מצוה is only דרבנן outside the מקדש, so they did. Today we do not take the לולב on a שבת first day because we are unsure of the date. Those who knew the date did take it, even after the חורבן, as two teachings show. The גמרא then brings the ברייתא on ״ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון״ as the source, which leads to a debate between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן over the word ״ביום״. The amud ends with a ברייתא trying to prove that סוכה applies at night. Two logical comparisons cancel each other out, and the verse that settles the question comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The fear of carrying four cubits, the same reason behind שופר and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes his reason for the גזירה. A person might carry the לולב ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים. The same reason explains why we do not blow שופר or read the מגילה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he will carry it four cubits in the public domain. And this is the reason for the שופר rule, and this is the reason for the מגילה rule.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts in the middle of רבה's explanation of why the לולב is not taken on שבת. He names the real danger, which is carrying in public, and says this one fear explains three different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full גזירה is this: a person might take the לולב in his hand and go to an expert to learn how to wave it or say the ברכה, and on the way he carries it ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים. Carrying in public is an איסור תורה. Because of that risk, the רבנן cancelled the מצוה on שבת. The same worry about going to an expert explains why שופר and מגילה are not done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: and he will carry it across
four cubits, the distance that makes carrying forbidden in a public area
the public domain
and this is the reason
מגילת אסתר, read on פורים

steps.whatToRemember: The one reason (fear of carrying ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים) covers three things: לולב, שופר, and מגילה on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that started on the previous amud. The beginning of the גזירה, about taking the לולב to an expert to learn, is in the earlier text.
steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה is the reason ראש השנה that falls on שבת has no שופר blowing, and why פורים never has the מגילה read on שבת.

phrases.english: and he will carry it four cubits
phrases.notes: Continues רבה's גזירה: he might take it to an expert to learn.

phrases.english: in the public domain.
And this is the reason for shofar,
phrases.notes: Why the שופר is not blown on שבת.

phrases.english: and this is the reason for the Megillah.
phrases.notes: Why the מגילה is not read on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה's answer on the previous amud, which explains why the לולב is not taken on שבת after the first day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן decreed against לולב, שופר, and מגילה on שבת because a person might carry the item ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים while going to learn from an expert.

steps.title: Then the first day should be banned too
steps.stepSummary: If the fear of carrying applies, it should apply on the first day of סוכות as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the first day too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's reason. The same worry should cancel the לולב on a first day that falls on שבת, yet the משנה allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear of carrying does not depend on which day of סוכות it is. Someone could just as easily carry the לולב on the first day. So רבה's reason seems to prove too much, because it would ban something the משנה permits.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
the first day (of סוכות)
also, too

phrases.english: If so,
the first day too!
phrases.notes: There should be a ban on the first day as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's reason by applying it to the first day.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's גזירה, given the משנה's rule that the לולב is taken on a שבת first day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fear of carrying is the same on every day, so the first day should also be banned.

steps.title: On the first day it was arranged to be taken at home
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made a rule that on the first day the לולב is taken at home, so there is no risk of carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first day, the רבנן instituted for it that it be taken in his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first day is different because of a special rule: people take the לולב at home. That removes the danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן arranged that on the first day each person takes the לולב in his own house. Since everyone already knows not to take it outside, he will not walk through the street with it. The risk is handled, so no ban is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: they instituted (made a rabbinic rule)
in his house

phrases.english: The first day,
the Rabbis instituted for it
phrases.notes: הָא here carries the sense of 'after all': the Rabbis already set this up.

phrases.english: that it be taken in his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רִאשׁוֹן, הָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן בְּבֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the first day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a rabbinic rule that removes the danger on the first day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first day carries the same risk of carrying as every other day.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תקנה to take the לולב at home removes the risk on the first day.

steps.title: What about the time before that rule was made?
steps.stepSummary: The home rule only explains things after it was made. Before it existed, the first day should have been banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well after the תקנה. Before the תקנה, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. There was a time before the home rule, and back then nothing protected the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule that the לולב is taken on a שבת first day seems to be older than this תקנה. Before the תקנה, the risk of carrying was fully present, yet the first day was still allowed. So the home rule cannot be the real reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well (only in one situation)
a rabbinic enactment
what is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well after the enactment,
before the enactment
what is there to say!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח אַחַר תַּקָּנָה, קוֹדֶם תַּקָּנָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the answer in step 3 does not cover every period of time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the home rule protects the first day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule came later, so before it existed the first day should have been banned, and it was not.

steps.title: New answer: first day is מן התורה everywhere, other days are not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier answer. On the first day the מצוה is מן התורה even in the גבולין, so the רבנן did not set it aside. On the other days it is only דרבנן there, so they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the first day, which is מן התורה in the גבולין, the רבנן did not decree against. These other days, which are not מן התורה in the גבולין, the רבנן did decree against.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אֶלָּא tells us the גמרא is giving up the home-rule answer and replacing it. The new difference is how strong the מצוה is on each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the מקדש, the Torah requires the לולב only on the first day. The other six days are a זכר למקדש, which is only דרבנן. The רבנן were willing to cancel their own rabbinic מצוה because of the carrying risk, but they would not cancel a מצוה that is מן התורה.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the earlier answer)
from the Torah, a biblical obligation
the outlying areas, everywhere outside the מקדש
they decreed
which are not (in effect)

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason is the strength of the מצוה. On the first day it is מן התורה everywhere, so there is no גזירה. On the other days it is only דרבנן outside the מקדש, so there is a גזירה.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not saying the first day has no risk of carrying. They are saying the risk was not enough to make them cancel a מצוה מן התורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: the רבנן are much more willing to set aside a rabbinic מצוה for a protective גזירה than a Torah מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, the first day, which is in effect
by Torah law in the outlying areas —
the Rabbis did not decree against it.
These other days, which are not in effect
by Torah law in the outlying areas —
the Rabbis decreed against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רִאשׁוֹן דְּאִיתֵיהּ מִן הַתּוֹרָה בִּגְבוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 4 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a new line between a Torah מצוה and a rabbinic one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first day was protected only by the home rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first day was never banned because it is a מצוה מן התורה in every place.

steps.title: Then we should take it on a שבת first day nowadays too
steps.stepSummary: If the first day is מן התורה, it should push aside the גזירה even today.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, nowadays too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new answer to ask a question about current practice. Today we do not take the לולב on a שבת first day, so why not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer says the רבנן do not cancel a Torah מצוה. The first day is still מן התורה today, so the same logic should mean taking the לולב even when it falls on שבת. Our practice seems to go against the answer just given.

keyTerms.meaning: nowadays, today

phrases.english: If so,
nowadays too!
phrases.notes: We should take the לולב on a שבת first day today as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer in step 5 against how people act today.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a Torah מצוה on the first day is not cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first day is still מן התורה today, so we should take the לולב even on שבת.

steps.title: We do not know exactly when the month was fixed
steps.stepSummary: Today we are not sure which day is truly the first day of סוכות, so it is not a definite Torah מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not know the fixing of the month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that people outside ארץ ישראל are not certain of the exact date. That doubt is enough to keep the גזירה in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the days of the גמרא, the month was set by בית דין based on witnesses. People far away were not sure which day had been chosen. So the day they keep as the first day might not really be the first day, and a doubtful Torah מצוה does not push aside the רבנן's גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: the fixing of the month (by בית דין)
we know

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about not knowing how to calculate a calendar. It is about not knowing which day בית דין actually declared as the new month.

phrases.english: We do not know
the fixing of the month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why we do not take the לולב on a שבת first day today.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a doubt about the facts that weakens the Torah obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Today's first day is a definite Torah מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the date is in doubt, today's first day is not a definite Torah מצוה, so the גזירה stands.

steps.title: Those who do know the date should take it on שבת
steps.stepSummary: People who know when the month was fixed should still take the לולב on a שבת first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They, who do know the fixing of the month, let them push aside שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the previous answer. It works only for people who are unsure, so those who know the date should take the לולב. The reply comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 7 depends on not knowing the date. People in ארץ ישראל, near בית דין, do know it. For them the first day is a definite Torah מצוה, so the reasoning of step 5 should let them take the לולב on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: they (those people)
let them push aside (שבת or the גזירה)

phrases.english: They, who do know
the fixing of the month,
let them override!
phrases.notes: Let them take the לולב on the first day even when it falls on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 7 does not cover everyone.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that doubt about the date is why the first day is not done on שבת today.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People who know the date have no doubt, so for them the first day is a definite Torah מצוה and should push aside the גזירה.

steps.title: Yes, those who know the date really did take the לולב on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees with the challenge: people who knew the true date did take the לולב on a שבת first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge from step 8 instead of pushing back. People who knew which day was truly the first day did take the לולב even when it fell on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 asked about people who know when the month was fixed. For them there is no doubt, so the first day is a definite Torah מצוה. The גמרא answers that this was in fact their practice, and the next step brings the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so. The גמרא accepts the point that was raised.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
phrases.notes: The גמרא admits the point. Those who knew the date did take the לולב on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by accepting its claim.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the challenger is correct and the practice matches it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the גזירה applied to everyone after the חורבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those who knew for certain which day was the first day did take the לולב on שבת.

steps.title: Proof from two teachings: Temple Mount versus synagogue
steps.stepSummary: One teaching says people brought their לולבים to הר הבית, and another says to the בית הכנסת. So the practice continued even after the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As one teaching says: When the first day of the חג falls on שבת, all the people bring their לולבים to הר הבית. Another teaching says: to the בית הכנסת. Learn from this: one teaching describes the time when the בית המקדש stood, and the other describes the time when it no longer stood. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the answer in step 9 by comparing two teachings that describe the same practice in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two teachings seem to disagree about where the לולבים were brought. The גמרא explains that הר הבית was the place while the בית המקדש stood, and the בית הכנסת was the place after it was destroyed. So even after the חורבן, people took the לולב on a שבת first day, as step 9 said.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple Mount.
The synagogue.
They bring or carry, done before שבת starts.
Learn from this. Used to introduce a conclusion and also to confirm it.
At the time when the בית המקדש is standing.

steps.confusionAlert: Bringing the לולבים happens on ערב שבת, before שבת begins. The point is not carrying on שבת. The point is that people prepared so they could take the לולב on שבת itself, and that this continued after the חורבן.

phrases.english: As it was taught in one source:
On the first festival day of the Festival
that falls on Shabbat,
all the people bring their lulavim
phrases.notes: They do this on Friday, before שבת.

phrases.english: to the Temple Mount.
And the other source taught: to the synagogue.
Learn from this:
Here, it refers to when the Temple is standing;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there, it refers to when the Temple is not standing.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual proof for the concession in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That people who knew the date took the לולב on a שבת first day even after the חורבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two teachings: one says the לולבים were brought to הר הבית, the other says to the בית הכנסת.
steps.whatToRemember: On the first day, the גזירה against taking the לולב on שבת applied only where the date was in doubt. Where the date was certain, people took the לולב on a שבת first day, even after the חורבן. On the other days of סוכות, the גזירה always applied outside the מקדש.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the first day is Torah law everywhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the לולב on the first day is מן התורה even outside the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That it is מן התורה even in the גבולין: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the claim from step 5 and asks for its source. It wants to know why the first day is a Torah מצוה even in the גבולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole explanation so far depends on this difference: the first day is Torah law everywhere, while the other days are Torah law only in the מקדש. Now the גמרא asks which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Areas outside the בית המקדש, meaning everywhere else.
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: That it applies by Torah law in the outlying areas:
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתֵיהּ מִן הַתּוֹרָה בִּגְבוּלִין מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new branch asking for the source of the claim in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that the לולב מצוה on the first day applies everywhere.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads each word of ״ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון״
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns several laws from the פסוק: each person must take his own לולב; it must belong to him; it applies even on שבת; it applies everywhere on the first day; and only the first day pushes aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: ״ולקחתם״ means each and every person must take one himself. ״לכם״ means from your own, which excludes a borrowed or stolen לולב. ״ביום״ means even on שבת. ״ראשון״ means even in the גבולין. ״הראשון״ teaches that only the first יום טוב pushes aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 11 with a ברייתא that learns a law from each word of the פסוק. The word ״ראשון״ is the source that the first day applies even in the גבולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that says ״ולקחתם... ביום הראשון״ does not name a place. So on the first day the מצוה applies everywhere. The extra letter ה in ״הראשון״ limits the rule that pushes aside שבת to the first day only.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall take. The plural form teaches that each person must take.
For yourselves, meaning the לולב must be your own.
Borrowed.
Stolen.
Pushes aside, here meaning it overrides שבת.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the main source for central הלכות of לולב: owning your own לולב on the first day, no stolen לולב, and the difference between the first day and the other days.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: And you shall take,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתְּהֵא לְקִיחָה בְּיַד כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: meaning there must be taking in the hand of each and every one.
For yourselves means from your own,
which excludes a borrowed or a stolen one.
On the day means even on Shabbat.
First means even in the outlying areas.
phrases.notes: This is the answer to step 11.

phrases.english: The first teaches

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹחֶה אֶלָּא יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: that it overrides Shabbat only on the first festival day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״ראשון״ in the פסוק has no place limit, so the first day is מן התורה even in the גבולין.

steps.title: Why would a verse be needed just to permit moving the לולב?
steps.stepSummary: Taking the לולב on שבת is only moving an object, which is at most a rabbinic issue. So why does the ברייתא need ״ביום״ to permit it on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: ״ביום״ means even on שבת. But it is only moving an object! Is a פסוק needed to permit just moving it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one line of the ברייתא, ״ביום״ means even on שבת, and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking up and shaking a לולב involves no מלאכה from the Torah. It is only טלטול, which the רבנן restricted. The Torah does not need a פסוק to permit something it never forbade, so the derivation from ״ביום״ seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. Used to quote an earlier statement in order to discuss it.
Moving or carrying an object around, with no מלאכה from the Torah.
Now, since. Introduces an obvious fact used to challenge.
Merely, just.

phrases.english: The Master said:
On the day means even on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again in order to analyze it.

phrases.english: Now, since it is merely moving an object,
is a verse needed to permit moving it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּיּוֹם וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּשַּׁבָּת מִכְּדֵי טִלְטוּל בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes one line of the ברייתא from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation ״ביום״ means even on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק is not needed to permit טלטול, since moving an object is not forbidden by the Torah.

steps.title: רבא: the verse permits preparing the לולב, following רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ״ביום״ permits the preparations of the לולב on שבת, following רבי אליעזר, who holds that the לולב and all its preparations push aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק is needed only for the preparations of the לולב, and it follows this תנא. As the ברייתא teaches: The לולב and all its preparations push aside שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers step 13. The פסוק is not about moving the לולב. It permits real מלאכות done to prepare the לולב, such as cutting it from the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Preparing a לולב can involve Torah-level מלאכות, so a פסוק is needed to permit them on שבת. This only works according to רבי אליעזר, who holds that the preparations of a מצוה push aside שבת just like the מצוה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Preparations of the לולב: the actions needed to get it ready, such as cutting it.
It is needed only for. Shows the true purpose of a פסוק or teaching.
According to this particular תנא.
The תנא who holds that the preparations of a מצוה push aside שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא means the לולב itself may be cut on שבת according to everyone. This is only the view of רבי אליעזר. Most חכמים disagree.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is needed only for the preparations of the lulav,
and according to this tanna,
as it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לוּלָב וְכׇל מַכְשִׁירָיו דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: The lulav and all its preparations override Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְמַכְשִׁירֵי לוּלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the scope of the derivation is changed and it is tied to a specific תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ביום״ comes to permit simple טלטול of the לולב on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״ביום״ permits Torah-level preparations of the לולב on שבת, following רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבי אליעזר uses for his view that the לולב and its preparations push aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said that רבא's answer follows רבי אליעזר. Now it asks where רבי אליעזר gets his idea from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said that ״ביום״ permits the preparations of the לולב on שבת, following רבי אליעזר. The גמרא now wants the פסוק-based reason behind his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The תנא who holds that the לולב and its preparations push aside שבת

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion that רבא relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches רבי אליעזר that the לולב overrides שבת.

steps.title: ״ביום״ means even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from the word ״ביום״ that the לולב applies on that day no matter what, even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ״on the day״, which means even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״ביום״ is רבי אליעזר's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ביום״ means 'on that very day, whatever day it is.' So the מצוה cannot be pushed off, even when the day is שבת. That is why its preparations override שבת too.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
On the day
And even on שבת

phrases.english: The verse says: "On the day,"
and even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״ביום״ teaches that the מצוה applies on its day even if that day is שבת.

steps.title: How do the רבנן use ״ביום״?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not agree that preparations push aside שבת. So what do they learn from ״ביום״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word ״ביום״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן, who disagree with רבי אליעזר, learn from the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. If the רבנן do not use ״ביום״ for שבת, it must teach them some other law.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי אליעזר
What do they do with it? (what do they learn from it?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis — this "on the day"
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי אליעזר to the other side of the debate.

steps.title: For the רבנן, ״ביום״ means day and not night
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״ביום״ to teach that the לולב is taken only during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to teach: ״by day״, and not at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn a time rule from ״ביום״: the לולב is a daytime מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word teaches a different law in each view. For רבי אליעזר it means 'even on שבת.' For the רבנן it means 'only by day, not at night.'

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
And not at night

phrases.english: They need it: "by day,"
and not at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn from ״ביום״ that the לולב is taken by day and not at night.

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר learn day and not night?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר used ״ביום״ for שבת. So where does he learn that the לולב is only by day?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, from where does he learn ״by day and not at night״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the opposite question. רבי אליעזר also agrees that the לולב is a daytime מצוה, so where does he get that from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree to the daytime rule. If רבי אליעזר used ״ביום״ for something else, he needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer — "by day and not at night"
from where does he derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question back onto רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי אליעזר's source for the daytime-only rule of לולב.

steps.title: From ״שבעת ימים״: days and not nights
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns the daytime rule from the end of the פסוק, ״seven days״, which means days and not nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the end of the פסוק: ״And you shall rejoice before ה׳ your God seven days״. The word 'days' means days, not nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר uses a different phrase in the same פסוק for the daytime rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״ימים״ (days) suggests only daytime. That frees up ״ביום״ for רבי אליעזר's שבת teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it
The end of the פסוק
Days and not nights

phrases.english: He derives it from the end of the verse:
"And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God
seven days" —
days and not nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״שבעת ימים״ teaches that the לולב is taken by day and not at night.

steps.title: Why the רבנן don't rely on ״ימים״
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן fear that ״ימים״ by לולב could be compared to ״ימים״ by סוכה, which includes nights. So they need ״ביום״ to make it clear that לולב is daytime only.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If we only had that phrase, I would have said: let us learn 'days' here from 'days' by סוכה. Just as there it means days and even nights, here too it means days and even nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן cannot learn the daytime rule from ״ימים״ alone, so they need ״ביום״ for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening word וְרַבָּנַן asks a brief question: why don't the רבנן use ״ימים״ like רבי אליעזר does? The answer is that ״ימים״ alone could be linked by a גזירה שוה to סוכה, where 'days' includes nights. So the רבנן need ״ביום״ to block that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an early assumption that gets corrected)
Let us learn it (by comparing two texts)
Just as there... so too here (the wording of a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of ״ימים״ here. By סוכה, 'days' includes nights. By לולב, the רבנן want it to mean days only. The whole worry is that one would be copied from the other.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis —
if it were from there, I would have said:
let us derive "days" "days" from sukka.
Just as there — days and even nights,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן נָמֵי יָמִים — וַאֲפִילּוּ לֵילוֹת.
phrases.english: so too here — days and even nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן's need for ״ביום״ against the source רבי אליעזר used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's choice not to learn the daytime rule from ״ימים״
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ימים״ by לולב could be compared to סוכה, which would make it days and nights.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן need ״ביום״ to teach clearly that לולב is days only.

steps.title: How do we know סוכה applies at night?
steps.stepSummary: Step 21 assumed that ״ימים״ by סוכה includes nights. The גמרא asks for the source of this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And סוכה itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check the assumption from step 21: where do we learn that the מצוה of סוכה applies at night too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about a גזירה שוה only works if 'days' by סוכה really includes nights. Now that starting point needs its own proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And sukka itself — from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption that step 21 depended on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the מצוה of סוכה applies at night as well.

steps.title: A ברייתא: ״ימים״ by סוכה includes nights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ״בסוכות תשבו שבעת ימים״ means days and even nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: ״In סוכות you shall dwell seven days״. 'Days' includes even nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that states the rule. The ברייתא will now defend this rule over the next few lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first states its conclusion: 'days' by סוכה includes nights. It then goes on to test that claim against other ways of reading the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (opens a ברייתא)
In סוכות you shall dwell

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"In sukkot you shall reside seven days" —
"days" — and even nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by quoting a ברייתא.

steps.title: Maybe סוכה should be like לולב, days only
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the opposite idea: compare 'days' by סוכה to 'days' by לולב, which is daytime only.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say 'days' includes nights? Or maybe it means only days and not nights? And this makes sense: 'days' is written here, and 'days' is written by לולב. Just as there it means days and not nights, so too here it means days and not nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own rule. It offers a comparison to לולב that would make סוכה a daytime-only מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both סוכה and לולב use the word 'days.' Since לולב is days only, this logic suggests that סוכה is also days only. That would go against the ברייתא's opening rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say... or perhaps it is only... (the ברייתא testing its own reading)
And it is logical (a reasoned argument)
It is said here... and it is said there (the wording of a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: Do you say "days" — and even nights,
or is it only "days" and not nights?
And it is logical:
"days" is stated here,
and "days" is stated regarding lulav;
just as there — "days" and not nights,
so too here — "days" and not nights.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר ״יָמִים״ וַאֲפִילּוּ לֵילוֹת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא ״יָמִים״ וְלֹא לֵילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's opening rule with a comparison to לולב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that סוכה applies at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה with לולב, which is days only, would make סוכה days only too.

steps.title: Or compare סוכה to the מלואים, days and nights
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers a competing comparison: the מלואים, where 'days' included nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: 'days' is written here, and 'days' is written by the מלואים. Just as there it means days and even nights, so too here it means days and even nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back with a different comparison. This one supports nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the seven days of the מלואים, the כהנים stayed at the אוהל מועד day and night, and the פסוק there also says 'days.' So this comparison would make סוכה days and nights. Now there are two possible comparisons that point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way (offering the opposite comparison)
The seven-day setting-up of the משכן and its כהנים

phrases.english: Or go this way:
"days" is stated here,
and "days" is stated regarding the inauguration.
Just as there — "days" and even nights,
so too here — "days" and even nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the לולב comparison with a comparison to the מלואים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows that the לולב comparison is not the only option, so it does not settle the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Another 'days' comparison exists that points to nights.

steps.title: סוכה is all day long, like the מלואים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that סוכה is closer to the מלואים: both are מצות that last all day, while לולב is done in a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which one it is similar to. We compare a thing whose מצוה lasts all day to another thing whose מצוה lasts all day. A thing whose מצוה takes only a moment should not be the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now tries to decide which comparison fits better. It brings a reason to choose the מלואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the סוכה and staying at the אוהל מועד both go on all day. Shaking a לולב is done once, in a moment. So סוכה seems more like the מלואים, which supports nights.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which one it resembles
We derive (compare one case to another)
And let it not be the proof
A single moment

phrases.english: Let us see to what it is similar:
we derive a matter whose מצוה is all day
from a matter whose מצוה is all day,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: and let a matter whose מצוה is one moment not prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks between the two comparisons in favor of the מלואים.
steps.raayaObject: That סוכה should be compared to the מלואים (days and nights)
steps.raayaSupportSource: Both סוכה and the מלואים are מצות that last all day, unlike לולב.

steps.title: But סוכה is for all generations, like לולב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back: סוכה and לולב both apply in every generation, while the מלואים happened only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: we compare a thing whose מצוה applies for all generations to another thing whose מצוה applies for all generations. The מלואים, which do not apply in later generations, should not be the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the last step with a different similarity that points back to לולב. Logic alone cannot decide, so the next step announces that a פסוק will settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכה and לולב are lasting מצות for every generation. The מלואים were a one-time event when the משכן was set up. This similarity favors לולב (days only), so the debate is now evenly balanced.

keyTerms.meaning: For all generations (a lasting מצוה)
Which are not in practice

steps.confusionAlert: This argument does not decide the question. Don't assume the last argument wins. In the next step the ברייתא turns to a פסוק to settle it, and the final הלכה is that סוכה does apply at night.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
we derive a matter whose מצוה is for all generations
from a matter whose מצוה is for all generations,
and let the inauguration not prove it,
which is not practiced for all generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 26's similarity with a competing similarity.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to compare סוכה to the מלואים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סוכה and לולב are both lasting מצות, while the מלואים were one-time. So לולב, which is days only, is the better match.

steps.title: Logic cannot decide, so the verse will settle it
steps.stepSummary: The two logical comparisons (to לולב or to the מלואים) ended in a tie. The ברייתא announces that a פסוק will decide the question instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא is getting ready to quote a verse that will decide whether סוכה applies at night. The verse itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 showed that סוכה is like the מלואים, because both last all day. Step 27 showed that סוכה is like לולב, because both apply in every generation. Since each comparison has an equal claim, logic alone cannot choose, so the ברייתא turns to the wording of the תורה to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": a formula that introduces a verse to prove or settle a point.
Logical reasoning. This is the method that just failed to settle the question.
A verse from the תורה. This is the source that will now decide the question.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect the answer in this line. "תלמוד לומר" only announces that a verse is coming. The actual verse and how it is used appear on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in a ברייתא. When two logical comparisons cancel each other out, the matter is decided by a verse instead. Here that verse will be the source that sitting in the סוכה applies at night too.

phrases.english: The verse states:
phrases.notes: Since logic can't decide which comparison is better, we learn it from the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the tie left by step 27. The logical arguments are set aside, and the ברייתא turns to the wording of the verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question will be settled by a פסוק, not by logical comparison. The specific verse follows on the next amud.
